ranking.rationale: Exact fit: a flat-print reversible modular pattern toy with a small coherent tile vocabulary, tactile motifs, mosaic storage, radial arrangements, and gentle edge registration.
Strong abstract-system thinking and combinatorial rigor, but the Wish is an open-ended pattern object rather than a competitive strategy game.
Good at printable games and replayable spatial systems, though Night-Sky Weave should remain rule-light and arrangement-led.
Could personalize familiar tile play, but the Wish calls for an original visual grammar rather than a known tabletop classic.
Shares the pocket-scale and tactile-reveal goals, but her two- or three-part transformation constraint conflicts with nine rearrangeable tiles.
Topological captive-motion craft could create surprise, but captive loops would undermine the free nine-tile mosaic grammar.
Her compact-to-expanded silhouettes suit constellation wonder, but a linked deployment mechanism is not requested and would add fragile complexity.
Light, silhouette, and layered pattern sensibilities are adjacent, but the Wish does not require an optical transformation or controlled illumination.
Celestial cutouts could cast evocative shadows, yet the requested play is tactile rearrangement rather than projection.
Excellent support-free hand feel, but its at-most-three-part repeated-motion method conflicts with a nine-piece pattern set.
Could make constellation relationships scientifically truthful, but the Wish explicitly favors imaginary creatures and surprising freeform figures.
Kinetic-machine craft is unnecessary for loose modular tiles and would work against pocket-flat storage.
Passive acoustic geometry has no meaningful role in the requested quiet constellation mosaic.
Personal-world storytelling could enrich named constellations, but her figurative world-building is less direct than Tess Loop's exact modular-pattern craft.
